name: Future trends

subjectOf.text: Integrating multimodal data from legal proceedings, combining text with audio and video such as courtroom transcripts, oral arguments, and visual cues, will make predictive analytics more robust by capturing richer case dynamics.
subjectOf.abstract: Future AI systems will analyze courtroom transcripts, oral arguments, and visual cues to provide richer insights into case dynamics.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: jurisdictions with diverse recorded data sources

subjectOf.text: Even as LLMs for judicial reasoning become more sophisticated, their inability to replicate empathy and social responsiveness will confine them to supportive rather than decisional functions.
subjectOf.abstract: However, AI's inability to replicate empathy and social responsiveness will limit its role to supportive functions.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: judicial reasoning and opinion drafting applications

subjectOf.text: Advanced artificial judicial intelligence capable of simulating full judicial processes remains speculative, and its feasibility is limited by ethical concerns including bias and accountability rather than by technical capability alone.
subjectOf.abstract: While current systems, like the Dutch court's traffic violation appeals tool, show promise, AAJI's feasibility is limited by ethical concerns, including bias and accountability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658
scope_conditions: full automation of judicial processes as opposed to decision support
